rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Results sections; the authors develop a procedure (maximum/minimum system head curves, 4,000 daily random demand curves, SOLVER pump selection) and apply it to a 127.7 ha on-demand citrus network in Valencia, reporting design discharges (218 L/s), energy consumption (Table 4) and annual total cost by pump combination (Fig. 15).
rows.notes: The study is a design/simulation exercise for dimensioning and regulating a pumping station in an on-demand network; it reports total annual costs (project plus energy) for different pump combinations and shows that dimensioning for maximum demand (256 L/s) rather than Cl<U+00E9>ment's discharge (166 L/s) raises reliability. It does not compare investment costs of on-demand networks against rotational or other delivery schedules, nor does it attribute higher investment cost to guaranteeing peak-period supply as its own finding. Model outputs are run on design data and are not checked against measurements from the real network, so under the rules they do not count as own evidence on the claim.

notes: Full text appears complete (pages 273-281). Text is OCR from a two-column layout with interleaved columns but is readable.
